goal: Each house crawl lane runs at least at its share of the 250 GB GeoNode month on prod, read the way the crawler Throughput dashboard on obs.virev.ai shows it, and Instagram re-reads meet the owner's goal on Crawler guy's board item p8. The duty moved from Crawler VP's d9 to Crawler guy's d8 on 11-24 (owner, t9), and its old lines (Instagram 10,000 profiles a minute, TikTok Shop 99.5% weekly coverage, Meta every due walk in 7 days) left that day, because 10,000 profiles a minute alone is about 20.8 TB a month. The split, from the 11-24 lane pricing page (prod crawler.proxy_wire_reads at the 11-01 to 11-09 pace): 250 GB less 40 GB for staging less 129 GB of prod paid and upkeep reads leaves 81 GB for prod house lanes, which ran 65,354 GB a month, so every house lane keeps 81 / 65,354 of its old pace. Census ran 23,979 GB, so it gets 29.7 GB; TikTok Shop 4,010 GB, so 4.97 GB; Meta Ads 1,583 GB, so 1.96 GB. GeoNode counts 1.1375 bytes per wire byte. One ok census profile read is 42,296 wire bytes (2.06 TB over 48.7M ok census jobs, 11-06 to 11-09), 48,112 counted; one ok TikTok Shop product row is 76,334 wire (974 GB over 12.8M rows), 86,830 counted; one Meta advertiser walk is 12,411 wire (16.4 GB a day over 1.32M walks a day), 14,118 counted. A month is 43,200 minutes, so the lines are 29.7 GB / 48,112 B / 43,200 = 14.3 Instagram profiles a minute, 4.97 GB / 86,830 B / 43,200 = 1.3 TikTok Shop good products a minute, and 1.96 GB / 14,118 B / 43,200 = 3.2 Meta advertiser walks a minute. Instagram counts instagram_account_snapshots and TikTok Shop its ok product rows, each in the slowest rolling hour of the last 6 h with the 5-minute slots under prod's deploy lock left out (deploy downtime is p6's number); Meta Ads reads advertiser walks finished over 24 h. TikTok Shop's 7-day coverage and Meta's walks due now stay in the run detail. Instagram re-reads read their goal from p8 at run time (owner 10-26 "1k+ every month, 10K+ every week" and "under 1k also monthly"): at most that share of read accounts with 10,000+ followers past 7 days, and of the rest past 30 days, two rows from page samples of instagram_census. At 48,112 B a read they cost about 21 TB a month (12.1M 10k+ accounts weekly and 386M others monthly), 84 times the whole plan, a decision for the owner. The census Postgres writer (Crawler VP's p895) is one more row: its worst lag over 24 h, in the 5-minute slots where Instagram profiles read at the plan line or more outside deploys, stays at most 5,000 records. The supporting metrics keep the rest of the owner's 10-19 duties: no Instagram queue backlogs, which is a 30-minute low over 80k records or growth over 6 h (p827), and every panel on the crawler dashboards draws. The lines are floors on each lane's share, and Search product, misc.'s d4 watches the month's total. GeoNode Mbps left this duty on 11-24 with the old lines. The census job failure share is reported in the run detail against the owner's 40 to 70% band, and a rise past it is an alert rule's job.

metrics.label: Crawl lanes under their share of the 250 GB plan, and p8 re-read rows missed
Instagram queues that backlog: over 80k at their 30-minute low, or grown over 6 h
Panels on the crawler dashboards on obs.virev.ai that show an error or No data

onMiss: For each missed metric, start or steer one live fix job this run, and keep it until the metric is met again. A live job that already owns the cause gets the numbers by message. Otherwise start one and put its fix step under the matching goal with duty "<id>/<metric>": the Instagram re-read rows go under p8, every other row under p6. throughput_goals_missed: the goal lines name each platform's rate against its goal; for each missed one find what stopped or slowed that crawl (a pause, a deploy, a hold, the proxy, a crashed role, a writer, a cadence control such as weekly_days or small_recheck_days) from the Throughput dashboard and logs, and get it back with a code or config fix through the crawler ops train, or a control write through /ops/controls with a measured reason. Bring a lane up to its plan line and no further: its line is its share of the 250 GB GeoNode month, so size its pool or interval to that rate and never write a coded cap (c239). The p8 re-read rows cost far more than the plan; fix a re-read miss only inside the census share and leave the gap to Crawler guy, who takes it to the owner. The census Postgres writer row: its line names the worst slot; read the census writer lane's process count (crawler_v3_runtime_role_processes{role="instagram-census-writer"}) and the lane scaler's last pass (crawler_v3_lane_scaler_last_pass_timestamp_seconds), then fix the writer or its scaler through the crawler ops train, never by holding the census rate down. ig_queues_growing_6h: name the queue and its consumer from the backlog line and fix the consumer. crawler_panels_blank: the dashboards line names each blank panel; fix its query in auto-sns-agent apps/infra/grafana/dashboards/crawler or the exporter it reads, or delete a panel nobody needs, and land it through the crawler ops train. A source_error comes first: fix the precheck read. The duty job itself only reads prod. All on target: end the turn with no message.
